full_judgment:
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of this petition, are that the respondents as plaintiff filed Title Suit No.59 of 1996 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Nalcity Court, Jhalakati contending inter alia that 7(seven) decimals land appertaining to CS Khatian No.6 under Plot No.--647415 belonged to Kolim Karigor who died leaving behind 2 sons, Alemuddin Karigor and Bidhai Karigor. Thereafter Alemuddin Karigor died leaving behind two daughters, Nur Banu and Jeil Banu. Nur Banu died leaving behind one son, Rustom Ali and two daughters, namely, Rokeya and Halima Begum. Thereafter, Jeil Banu died leaving behind her husband Entazuddin and only son in Harun. Rustom Ali, Rokeya Khatun, Halima Begum. Entazudin and Harun transferred two decimals land from Plot No.454 / 835 under CS Khatian No.06 on 29.02.1996 vide registered deed No.357 at a consideration of taka 4,000.00 in favour of the plaintiff and they gave possession long 40 years ago to the plaintiff and since then the plaintiff has been possessing the land and running his business therein by erecting tin-shed construction and the defendant has no right title in the said two decimal land. 

 3. The further case of the plaintiff is that the deed writer committed wrong in writing the description of scheduled land; as a result, the plaintiff again obtained a rectification deed duly registered on 20.03.1997. The land of Plot No. 454 / 833 has been wrongly recorded in the name of defendant Nos.17-21 under RS Khatian Nos.120/123 corresponding to SA Nos.103/83. The plaintiff has been possessing the suit land for more than 40 years. Some of the defendants claimed title in the suit land on 25 Magh, 1402 BS; as a result, a cloud has been cast upon the title of the plaintiff and hence the case. 

 4. Defendant Nos.18 and 20 along with defendant No.19 contested the suit by filing written statement denying all material allegations contending, inter alia, that the superior landlord settled the land under CS Khebot Nos.33, 34, 36, 47, and 50 including Amirabad Hat and the suit land to the predecessor of the defendants and others and delivered possession of the settled land including the suit land before RS operation. Koram Ali, predecessor of the defendants erected shop there and during R.S and SA operation, one decimal land has been correctly recorded in the name of Koram Ali in Plot No. 454 / 835 of R.S. Khatian No.123 corresponding to SA Khatian No. 103 and after the death of Koram Ali, the said land devolved upon the defendants and they have been possessing the same on payment of rent to the Government and the plaintiff has no right, title and interest in the said land. 

 9. Mr. Md. Jahangir Kabir, learned Advocate, appearing for the petitioners, submits that the RS and the SA Khatians in respect of 1(one) decimal land in Plot No. 454/ 835 has been recorded in the name of Koram Ali, predecessor of the defendants and the plaintiff could not rebut the correctness of the said Khatian, but the learned appellate Court without reversing those findings allowed the appeal thus committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that the learned trial Court found that the record of suit land does not stand in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff in the RS and the SA Khatian and as such, the heirs of Nur Banu and Jeil Banu had no right to sell the suit land in favour of the plaintiff, but the appellate Court in allowing the appeal committed an error of law occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that in view of the findings that there are defects in the deeds (exhibit nos.4 and 5) of the plaintiff in spite of that the appellate Court committed an error of law by allowing the appeal. He further submits that the trial Court found that PW1 stated in his cross-examination that the name of deed giver of the plaintiff was not recorded in the RS and the SA record and PW3 stated in his cross-examination that the father of defendant No.18 is the owner of the studio and PW4 stated in his cross-examination that they did not file any suit against uncorrected record, but the appellate Court below by allowing the appeal committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submits that defendant. Nos.18-20 along with 17(ka) to 17(Ja) obtained this suit land through inheritance and they are still in possession on the suit land and earlier the predecessor of the said defendants obtained the suit land through settlement (pattan) from earlier owner and the name of the predecessor of the said defendants was recorded in the SA and the RS Khatians correctly and the said defendants are still in possession of the suit land and the plaintiff has no possession in the suit land, but the appellate Court below committed an error of law. He further submits that the trial Court found that as per SA Khatian Nos.103 and 83, the said SA record was made in the names of the father of defendant Nos.18- 20 along with the name of dead defendant No.17 in respect of the suit land; that the said defendant mainly claimed that the land under earlier Plot No. 415/647 and the plaintiff claimed land Hal Plot No.454/647 are not same land. On the other hand, the plaintiff claimed that both the land under those plots are same, but in respect of this, the plaintiff did not prove the same through any Advocate Commissioner and the plaintiff did not also prove the same through filing the plot Index in respect of the suit land, but the Court of appeal below committed an error of law by allowing the appeal. He further submits that the trial Court found that the plaintiff's alleged deeds were made as per RS and SA record, but wherein the names of the deed given is absent, so the said alleged deeds are illegal and ineffective. He further submits that the SA and the RS records were prepared in the name of Koram Ali in respect of the suit land who was the father of defendants Nos.18-20. The rent of the suit land was paid by said Koram Ali till 1418 to 1419 B.S. dated 14.06.2013 and subsequently, the said rent of the suit land was paid by defendant No.18, Nurul Islam till 1425 BS dated 23.01.2018 and defendant Nos.18-20 are the successors of said Karam Ali, whose name was recorded in SA and RS record properly and as per pattan, SA and RS records along with plot Index, the instant petitioners are bona fide owners and possessors of the suit land. He further submits that the High Court Division considered some citations regarding question of limitation. He further submits that the judgment and decree suffers from gross illegality and legal infirmity and as such, the same is not sustainable in law and liable to be set aside. 

 12. We have gone through all those evidence on record and see therefrom that nothing cogent could be elicited to disbelieve the PWs. The trial Court found that in spite of denial of PW1, the other PWs admitted that there was a studio in the suit land of the defendants and they were running business therein. But we have gone through the testimonies of the PWs and found that they have admitted the fact of existence of a studio of defendants but the same is situated the Amirabad Bazar but not in the suit land. DWs 1 and 2 stated that the plaintiff had shop in the market. DWs 3, 4 and 5 in cross-examination deposed that the plaintiff had shop in the suit land. From the evidence of PWs and DWs, it appears to us the existence of the plaintiffs shop in the suit land stands as admitted fact. The entry of hal or SA Khatian is made in the names of vendors of the plaintiffs. The trial Court held that without correcting the names of vendors, the transfer of the suit property was illegal and null and void. The trial Court further held that although it is proved that the plaintiff has a shop in the Amirabad market, it is not proved whether it is in the suit property or not. For those reasons, the suit was dismissed. But we find from the testimonies of the witnesses that they have deposed that the plaintiffs shop is situated in the suit land. 

 13. The appellate Court found that Rustam Ali, Rokeya Begum, Halima Khatun, Antazuddin and Harun through a deed dated 20.03.1997 transferred .01 decimal land of SA Khatian No.83, Hal Dag No.454 and .01 decimal land of SA Khatian No.103, Hal Dag No.454/835 in total .02 decimals land in favour of the plaintiff and that the plaintiff has established a shop and has been running his business.
